To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The theory of bilocal wave functions is developed for the description of the inner structure of electrons.

the inner structure of electrons and other elementary particles can be described by means of the bilocal wave functions, that the inner interactions are of a Coulomb-Darwin type, and that the energy values are finite.

(1) the mass of the electron can be decomposed into a mass that can be explained by electromagnetic theory and a fundamental mass that cannot be explained by electromagnetic interactions; (2) the fundamental mass of the electron has a value of 1.007 277 037 5(4) GeV/c2; (3) the fundamental charge of the electron has the value of the proton charge, 1.007276466583(10) times the proton charge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an approach to the problem of quantum electrodynamics which is based on a nonrelativistic theory of elementary particles.
the problem of finding an adequate theory of the internal interactions between electrons and quarks.
the development of the quantum mechanics of a system of particles in a nonrelativistic field theory of elementary particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory has been successful in providing a consistent description of the internal structure of elementary particles, which includes their mass, spin and magnetic moment.

the bilocal theory of the electron, in its present state, is not yet a satisfactory theory, but that it is a promising one, and that it should be pursued further, especially with the aim of clarifying the problem of the ground state.

the bilocality of the wave functions of electrons is not only a mathematical fiction, but that it also is a physical reality which has to be taken into account in the interpretation of the quantum mechanical wave function of electrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it has been shown that there are no diverging terms in the Hamiltonian of a particle interacting with the electromagnetic field, if one uses the bilocal theory.
the bilocal wave functions of the electrons in the atom are not a good approximation for the real wave function.
the theory of bilocal wave functions, as developed in this thesis, is a new and successful theory of the internal interaction in elementary particles.

, for a given set of initial conditions, we can use the quantum wavefunction to predict the probability of finding the system in a particular state at a later time.
there is a fundamental difference between the quantum theory of a single electron and the quantum theory of an electron in a hydrogen atom.
the energy of a particle can be calculated from the mass of the particle and the energy of the particle's internal interactions.
